D3·1h9d — 2026-09-17
chose: 1.2 CONTRACT (rule fidelity). (a) decision_logged gains `quote?`: the operator's own words the rule came from, copied exactly, non-empty, at most 300 chars, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). (b) A pure core/rule-fidelity.ts lists a rule's SPECIFICS: HTTP status codes and classes (400, 4xx), paths (a token with `/` between word characters, or a file name with an extension), and values (backticked spans, double-quoted spans, tokens carrying a digit). It then reports the specifics the quote lacks, by case-insensitive whitespace-collapsed substring. (c) Standing constraints renders each quoted rule as `- [D<n>] <rule> — operator: "<quote>"`, plus ` (not in the operator's words: <specifics>)` when any are missing. The header becomes `Standing constraints — obey verbatim; where a rule quotes the operator, the quote decides (<N>):` ONLY when an in-force rule carries a quote, so quote-less records render byte-identically. decisions.md and the review packet render the quote too. (d) sofar_log_decision returns `warnings[]`, and `sofar event append --type decision_logged` prints them, naming the unquoted specifics; never a refusal. (e) The `rule` and `quote` descriptions and the CLI dialect's fields teach: word the rule as the operator did, and pass their words as quote. Guard notices in hooks are unchanged in 1.2.
over: Refusing a rule that adds specifics (a paraphrase that rightly names a file would cost a retry, and the plan says warn); recording prompts so the quote can be verified mechanically (user content in the record); rendering the quote instead of the rule (the operator's sentence often lacks the context the rule supplies); clipping long quotes at render (a clipped quote can drop the clause that matters, so the cap sits at validation)
because: Round 1's only Claude quality miss was lost at capture. The operator said "Reject anything else"; the agent's rule added "with 4xx"; the "obey verbatim" header made that paraphrase law, so S9 returned 400 and failed A6. Keeping the operator's words beside the rule, and flagging what the rule adds in every digest, puts the source in front of each later session at zero extra calls. The write-time warning lets the capturing session correct the rule the moment it logs it. Frozen prediction: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.
